## asset.delete

Deletes an asset: moves its file, .meta and cached import to the project's trash (.strata/Trash) and removes it from the project, in one undo step (edit.undo restores it with the same handle, so references to it work again, as long as the edited scene stays: opening or creating another clears the undo history; the trash keeps the files for 30 days). Fails while scenes, prefabs, models, materials or the open scene use it or the project names it (its start or loading scene, the game's icon, its settings), listing them in the error's data (referencedBy, as asset.findReferences returns it); force: true deletes it anyway, leaving those references missing. The open scene itself cannot be deleted. Returns {asset, path, trash, referencedBy}.

Kind: `Edit` · Results: `Content` · MCP toolsets: `assets` · Answers later (MayDefer): no · Waits for the asset scan: yes · Registered at `StrataEditor/src/Editor/EditorAssetCommands.cpp:930`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `asset` | string | yes |   | Asset to delete (asset handle, or path relative to the asset directory). |
| `force` | boolean | no |   | Delete although other assets or the open scene use it (default false). |

<details>
<summary>Parameter schema of asset.delete</summary>

  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "asset": {
      "description": "Asset to delete (asset handle, or path relative to the asset directory)",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "force": {
      "description": "Delete although other assets or the open scene use it (default false)",
      "type": "boolean"

  },

## asset.deleteFolder

Deletes a folder with everything in it: moves it to the project's trash (.strata/Trash) and removes its assets from the project, in one undo step (edit.undo restores it, every asset with its handle, as long as the edited scene stays; the trash keeps it for 30 days). Fails while assets outside the folder or the open scene use an asset in it, listing them in the error's data (referencedBy); force: true deletes it anyway. Fails when it holds the open scene. ## asset.import

Copies external files and folders into the project and imports them in the background: the editor keeps running, and the command answers when every import is done. A file goes into &#96;directory&#96; (&quot; (n)&quot; added when its name is taken) with the files it reads (a glTF model's buffers and images, in a new folder named after it, keeping their layout); a folder goes there with its tree (asset files, their .meta files, what its models read). Returns {asset, path, name, type (of the first file's asset), items: \[{source, path, folder, assets: \[{asset, path, type}\], error?, rolledBack?}\]}. Fails (Failed) when an import failed, with the items in the error's data; the failed files are removed again unless keepOnFailure. wait: false answers at once ({importing: true}); asset.info tells when an asset is imported.

Kind: `Edit` · Results: `Content` · MCP toolsets: `core`, `assets` · Answers later (MayDefer): yes · Waits for the asset scan: yes · Registered at `StrataEditor/src/Editor/EditorAssetCommands.cpp:788`

| `files` | array of string | no |   | Absolute paths of files to import. |
| `keepOnFailure` | boolean | no |   | Keep the files of failed imports in the project, with their errors (default false: they are removed). |

## asset.info

An asset's metadata, load state, import errors and warnings, sub-assets, import settings with the description of every setting (importSettingsProperties: type, range, options; what asset.setImportSettings accepts) and whether an import is running. Meshes, models and prefabs add bounds: {min, max, size}, what they draw around their origin as an instance placed there (skinned characters in their rest pose): use it to check a model's size before placing it. When meshes or skeletons it needs are not loaded, asset.info loads them and answers once they are in (at most about 300 frames; then boundsPending: true); bounds: false answers at once without bounds.

## asset.move

Moves or renames an asset (with its .meta and cached import) within the asset directory; its handle and every reference to it stay valid. One undo step (edit.undo moves it back); a name that differs only in case renames it in place, and its own path changes nothing. Fails when another file is at the path. ## asset.place

Places a prefab, model or mesh where a ray, a Scene view pixel or a point lands, resting on the surface there, as a drop into the Scene view does. One undo step. Exactly one of: ray {origin, direction}; viewport {x, y, width?, height?} (a pixel of the Scene view's image through its camera, as scene.raycast); point \[x, y, z\] with normal (default \[0, 1, 0\]), e.g. a scene.raycast hit. A ray or pixel that hits nothing lands on the grid plane y = 0 within 500 m, else on the ray at fallbackDistance (default 10 m; for a pixel the editor camera's distance to its target), unless requireSurface: then it fails. snap (meters) puts the point on that grid along the surface and finds the height there; rotation (\[x, y, z\] degrees) and scale (uniform) apply over the asset's own. A mesh becomes an entity with a Mesh Renderer, named after it. While the prefab or model loads it waits (at most 30 s), then up to 5 s for what its size needs (after that it places by the size known so far: bounds.pending true). Returns {id (the root), entities (every root), placedOn: surface \| grid \| inFront \| point, hitEntity (null unless surface), point, normal, translation, bounds {min, max, size, center, pending}, snapped}; while playing it changes the running copy only.

Kind: `Edit` · Results: `Content` · MCP toolsets: `scene` · Answers later (MayDefer): yes · Waits for the asset scan: yes · Registered at `StrataEditor/src/Editor/Commands/PlacementCommands.cpp:463`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `asset` | string | yes |   | The prefab, model or mesh to place (asset handle, or path relative to the asset directory). |
| `fallbackDistance` | number | no |   | With ray: where on the ray an asset lands when nothing is hit and the grid is beyond 500 m (default 10). Value: at least `0.5`, at most `500.0`. |
| `maxDistance` | number | no |   | With ray or viewport: how far the ray looks for a surface, in meters (default: unlimited, or the view's far plane). Value: more than `0`. |
| `normal` | array of number | no |   | With point: the surface's normal there (default \[0, 1, 0\]). Items: at least 3, at most 3. |
| `parent` | string or null | no |   | Parent of the placed roots; null or omitted for the top level (entity ID or null). |
| `point` | array of number | no |   | Place resting on this point, e.g. a scene.raycast hit (one of ray, viewport, point). Items: at least 3, at most 3. |
| `ray` | object | no |   | Place where this ray lands (one of ray, viewport, point). |
| `ray.direction` | array of number | yes |   | Where it points; any length but zero. Items: at least 3, at most 3. |
| `ray.origin` | array of number | yes |   | Where the ray starts, in world space. Items: at least 3, at most 3. |
| `requireSurface` | boolean | no |   | Fail instead of falling back to the grid or the ray when nothing is hit (default false). |
| `rotation` | array of number | no |   | Euler angles in degrees over the asset's own rotation (default \[0, 0, 0\]). Items: at least 3, at most 3. |
| `scale` | number | no |   | Uniform scale over the asset's own (default 1). Value: more than `0`, at most `1000.0`. |
| `snap` | number | no |   | Grid step in meters: the point snaps to it along the surface, and the height is found there. Value: more than `0`, at most `10000.0`. |
| `viewport` | object | no |   | Place where this pixel of the Scene view lands, through its camera (one of ray, viewport, point). |
| `viewport.height` | integer | no |   | The height of that image (default: the Scene view's, or 720). Value: at least `1`, at most `16384`. |
| `viewport.width` | integer | no |   | The width of the image the pixel refers to (default: the Scene view's, or 1280 while it has none). Value: at least `1`, at most `16384`. |
| `viewport.x` | number | yes |   | Pixels from the image's left edge, continuous: the middle of the first column is 0.5. |
| `viewport.y` | number | yes |   | Pixels from the image's top edge, continuous. |

## asset.setBudget

Sets the asset streaming budgets of the open project's asset manager (until the project closes; not undoable; fails without a project): resident memory per pool in megabytes (1 MB = 1048576 bytes; assets over budget are evicted, least recently used first), the megabytes of loads in flight, the GPU megabytes uploaded per frame, the main-thread milliseconds finalization may take per frame, the milliseconds its upload steps may take (writing staging memory; steps are sized to fit) and the staging megabytes texture and mesh uploads may hold (sustained uploads reach at most half of the staging per frame, so raise both for a loading screen), and the megabytes imports may take together (importMB: their memory estimates; default a quarter of physical memory, 1-4 GB). Values must be greater than 0; reset: true starts from the defaults (derived from the GPU). Returns the budgets in effect (bytes, null = unlimited).

Kind: `Session` · Results: `Content` · MCP toolsets: `streaming` · Answers later (MayDefer): no · Waits for the asset scan: no · Registered at `StrataEditor/src/Editor/EditorStreamingCommands.cpp:218`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cpuMB` | number | no |   | Resident CPU memory of asset data, in MB. Value: more than `0`. |
| `finalizeMsPerFrame` | number | no |   | Main-thread milliseconds finalization may take per frame. Value: more than `0`. |
| `gpuBuffersMB` | number | no |   | Resident GPU buffer (mesh) memory, in MB. Value: more than `0`. |
| `gpuTexturesMB` | number | no |   | Resident GPU texture memory, in MB. Value: more than `0`. |
| `importMB` | number | no |   | Memory imports may take together by their estimates, in MB: an import that does not fit beside those that run waits for them (one runs alone even when it exceeds it). Value: more than `0`. |
| `inFlightMB` | number | no |   | Stored bytes of loads being read, decoded or waiting to be finalized, in MB. Value: more than `0`. |
| `reset` | boolean | no |   | Start from the default budgets before applying the given values (default false). |
| `stagingMB` | number | no |   | Staging memory texture and mesh uploads may hold, in flight and idle, in MB. Value: more than `0`. |
| `uploadMBPerFrame` | number | no |   | GPU bytes finalization uploads per frame, in MB. Value: more than `0`. |
| `uploadMsPerFrame` | number | no |   | Main-thread milliseconds the upload steps of a frame may take (writing staging memory, recording copies). Value: more than `0`. |

## asset.setImportSettings

Changes import settings (merged into the current ones; asset.info lists every setting with its type, range or options), saves the .meta and imports the asset again in the background, without blocking the editor. Returns when the import is done (settings, warnings) and fails when it failed; wait: false returns at once. Unknown settings, invalid values and numbers outside a setting's range change nothing (they are refused, never clamped).

Kind: `Edit` · Results: `Content` · MCP toolsets: `assets` · Answers later (MayDefer): yes · Waits for the asset scan: yes · Registered at `StrataEditor/src/Editor/EditorAssetCommands.cpp:1084`

| `settings` | object | yes |   | Settings to change, e.g. {&quot;MaxSize&quot;: 1024} for a texture or {&quot;Scale&quot;: 0.01} for a model. |
| `wait` | boolean | no |   | Return when the import is done (default true). |

## asset.stats

Asset memory and streaming: resident bytes and budget per pool (cpu, gpuTextures, gpuBuffers; null budget = unlimited), load counts, the streaming queue (queued loads per priority, loads and bytes in flight), finalization (GPU bytes uploaded and main-thread milliseconds, and of those the milliseconds of the upload steps, last frame and maximum of recent frames, with their budgets and the staging budget), evictions (and how many resident assets eviction looked at), cancellations, staging releases and dependency prefetches (prefetch: loads of what assets reference started when their reads completed, and those dropped on arrival for lack of room in the budgets) and mip streaming (mipStreaming: loads of only a texture's header and smallest levels, reads of further levels queued and completed, levels raised and dropped (and of those dropped, the levels a budget took: its pressure, or room for detail a view needs more), bytes read for them in all and in the last frame, textures below the level their views need, and textures reading or changing levels now), and importMemoryMB (the imports' memory estimates: admitted, budget, queued). With assets: true it also lists the assets that are resident, loading, failed or pinned, with their memory, state, last use and pins; streaming textures add residentMip (the finest mip level resident, 0 the full resolution), wantedMip (the finest level their views need), mipCount and residentBytes (what the resident levels hold). geometryPool is the renderer's pool of every mesh's GPU geometry (usedMB, capacityMB, allocations, fragmentation of its free space, moves and growths so far; null without a GPU): meshes count their ranges of it as gpuBuffers.

Kind: `Query` · Results: `Session` · MCP toolsets: `streaming` · Answers later (MayDefer): no · Waits for the asset scan: no · Registered at `StrataEditor/src/Editor/EditorStreamingCommands.cpp:164`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `assets` | boolean | no |   | Also list the assets (default false). |
| `limit` | integer | no |   | At most this many assets in the list (default 100). Value: at least `1`, at most `1000000`. |
| `sort` | string | no |   | Order of the list: &quot;bytes&quot; (most memory first, the default) or &quot;lastUsed&quot; (most recently used first). One of: `bytes`, `lastUsed`. |

## asset.types

The asset types this editor knows, each with the extension of the documents the engine writes for it (nativeExtension, null for types only imported) and its importers: {name, version (raised whenever its output changes, which imports the type's files again), extensions (lower case, with the dot)}. Types without importers (Mesh, Skeleton, AnimationClip) are sub-assets a model's import makes, as it makes its materials and textures. Needs no project.
